sections.html:
Spalding County divides the work among five bodies. The Tax Commissioner owns the bill and the payment window. The assessors value property and approve exemptions, and a Grand Jury appointed board of equalization settles disputes. Millage rates come from the commissioners and the school board.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, three blocks from the courthouse. The phone is (770) 467-4360 and the mailbox is PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. Call (770) 467-4240 for the Tax Assessor. County administration works from 119 E. Solomon Street. The Tax Commissioner's office opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

Bills for land, buildings and business equipment normally fall due on November 15. Late fees do not start until 60 days after the bills go out. After the due date the county adds interest monthly at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty accrues every 120 days up to 20%.

Homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty. Mobile homes sit on an April 1 schedule with a location permit, and the office can levy on unpaid property as a last resort.

sections.h2: Spalding County tax rules at a glance
sections.html:
Spalding County property tax rules
TopicRule
Assessed value40% of fair market value
Return seasonOpens January 1 and closes April 1
Land and building billsDue November 15
Appeal cutoffForty-five days after the notice mailing date
Homestead filingApplication in hand before April 1 earns the exemption for that tax year
Mobile home taxDue April 1
Delinquent tax salesHeld on a first Tuesday, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

A mill is one thousandth of a dollar per dollar of assessed value. Exemptions come off the 40% assessed value first, and the millage rate applies to what remains.

sections.h2: How to contest a Spalding County value
sections.html:
You have forty-five days after the assessment notice goes out. Argue taxability, value or uniformity, and leave the size of the bill out of it. The assessors review first; the next stops are the equalization board or arbitration, then Superior Court.

The county sometimes stretches the homestead filing window to match the appeal period in a given year, so watch the notice for dates. Exemptions based on income have to be requested in person with proof of the prior year's income.

The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly: age 65 before January 1, net income capped at $15,000, with bigger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption: age 62 or older, or totally disabled at any age, with household gross income capped at $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating school exemption for owners 65 and up, which freezes the value used for school tax.

An approved exemption carries forward until the owner moves, so a buyer applies fresh for the new address. Owners 62 and up with household income below $15,000 may have a deferral on file; the Tax Commissioner can confirm for your parcel.

Spalding County has 70,775 people as of mid-2025, a 5.2% rise from the 2020 base, living among 29,850 housing units. Owners occupy 62.7% of units, and 20.6% of residents are 65 or older, which puts the senior exemptions above in play for many sellers.

The middle home value is $228,700, median gross rent is $1,113 a month, and median household income is $62,071.

Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk all sit. Heirs selling an inherited house can reach the county Probate Court at (770) 467-4341.

1. Call the Tax Commissioner at (770) 467-4360 for your parcel's balance, including interest and any penalty.
  2. Check with the Tax Assessor at (770) 467-4240 that your homestead exemption is on file, and tell a buyer it will not carry over, since they must apply for their own.
  3. Look at the notice of assessment. If the forty-five day appeal period is still open and the value looks high, file before it closes.
  4. If the house is outside Griffin and you plan repairs, call Community Development about permits first.
  5. Ask the closing attorney to show the tax proration on the settlement statement.

The bill goes to whoever owns the property on January 1, so a sale after that date means the contract has to say how the November bill is shared. A cash buyer will usually agree to a straightforward split and pay off any tax balance at closing.

Georgia law puts delinquent tax sales on a month's first Tuesday, within a 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. window. The sale takes place at 411 E. Solomon Street. Bidder rules:

  • Register on sale morning between 8:00 and 9:30.
  • Be at least 18 years old.
  • Show a driver's license or other official ID.

Bidding usually starts around 10:00 or 10:30.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

When you sell a house with back taxes, ask for a payoff that includes interest and penalties, and have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds. That clears the lien risk and lets the buyer take clean title, and it keeps the closing from stalling at the last minute.

The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds, at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin. Call 770-467-4309 to reach the clerk, whose staff includes a deputy for real estate. The clerk's office is also where to get a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. The Planning Commission gathers on the last Tuesday evening of each month, and the Board of Appeals follows on the second Thursday, both at 6:00 p.m. in the Courthouse Annex. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. It has a permit technician and a business and alcohol license technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County payment deadline?
faqs.a: November 15, for bills on land, buildings and business personal property. Late fees wait until 60 days after the bills are mailed.

faqs.q: What is the appeal cutoff after a Spalding County assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice is mailed. Assessors review first, then the equalization board or an arbitrator, and finally Superior Court.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County late penalty?
faqs.a: Once November 15 passes, interest accrues each month, and penalties climb in 5% steps every 120 days to 20%. Homesteaded parcels with less than $500 due skip the penalty.

faqs.q: Where is the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, phone (770) 467-4360. It opens at 8:00 on weekdays and closes at 4:30.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spalding County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, though the Tax Commissioner can levy on unpaid property and sell it at a tax sale. Request a payoff figure that includes interest and penalties so the balance can be settled from your closing proceeds.
